demo.why.first_stage_engine: The first-stage engines lift everything off the pad. They set thrust, efficiency, cost and risk for the whole climb.
demo.why.upper_stage_engine: The upper-stage engine finishes the climb in vacuum and places the satellite into its orbit.
demo.why.fairing: The fairing shields the satellite through the atmosphere, then must separate cleanly.
demo.why.engine_hot_fire: A hot-fire test costs time and money but can catch a flaw before flight.
demo.predict.vac_isp: Which of these engines is the most efficient in vacuum?
demo.trivia.fairing.prompt: Two NASA climate satellites, OCO (2009) and Glory (2011), were lost. What failed?
demo.trivia.fairing.b: The solar wings did not open
demo.trivia.fairing.c: The upper stage ran out of fuel
demo.notice.briefing: Earth Watch: put a 150 kg imaging satellite into a 550 km sun-synchronous orbit.
demo.notice.build: Build begins. First decision: the first-stage engine.
demo.notice.frr: Flight Readiness Review. FLIGHT polls every console.
demo.notice.nogo: A console called NO-GO. Talk it through, then FLIGHT polls again.
demo.notice.maxq: Approaching Max Q. STRUCT, watch the load.
demo.notice.coverage: Out of ground-station coverage. Telemetry resumes at the next pass.
demo.event.liftoff: Lift-off! All engines at full thrust.
demo.event.meco: Main engine cut-off and stage separation.
demo.build.test_pass: Hot-fire test passed. No flaw found: reliability +1 %.
demo.build.test_skipped: Hot-fire test skipped. The risk stays hidden.
demo.issue.twr_low: Lift-off thrust-to-weight is below 1.2. Add engines or choose a stronger engine.
demo.warning.twr: Lift-off TWR would fall below 1.0 with the planned engine count.
